pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: drm/amdgpu: new queue policy, take first 2 queues of each pipe v2 Instead of taking the first pipe and giving the rest to kfd, take the first 2 queues of each pipe. Effectively, amdgpu and amdkfd own the same number of queues. But because the queues are spread over multiple pipes the hardware will be able to better handle concurrent compute workloads. amdgpu goes from 1 pipe to 4 pipes, i.e. from 1 compute threads to 4 amdkfd goes from 3 pipe to 4 pipes, i.e. from 3 compute threads to 4 v2: fix policy comment This change requires next two following it. Otherwise the GPU will hang. BUG=b:66735140 TEST=boot Kahlee, run graphics_SanAngeles CQ-DEPEND=I8b536c3775e971152271292e06caa13dc733253b Reviewed-by: Edward O'Callaghan <funfunctor@folklore1984.net> Reviewed-by: Felix Kuehling <Felix.Kuehling@amd.com> Acked-by: Christian Knig <christian.koenig@amd.com> Signed-off-by: Andres Rodriguez <andresx7@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com> (cherry picked from commit 0a281f5a2cba94a574167edadca88a3130a88612) Signed-off-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Change-Id: I51e62f14f2b26bbdf02590d59fa758a28af37eb6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/738949 Commit-Ready: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Tested-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/amdgpu/gfx9: new queue policy, take first 2 queues of each pipe Instead of taking the first pipe and giving the rest to kfd, take the first 2 queues of each pipe. Effectively, amdgpu and amdkfd own the same number of queues. But because the queues are spread over multiple pipes the hardware will be able to better handle concurrent compute workloads. amdgpu goes from 1 pipe to 4 pipes, i.e. from 1 compute threads to 4 amdkfd goes from 3 pipe to 4 pipes, i.e. from 3 compute threads to 4 gfx9 was missed when this patch set was rebased to include gfx9. UPSTREAM: drm/amdgpu: workaround tonga HW bug in HQD programming sequence Tonga based asics may experience hangs when an HQD's EOP parameters are modified. Workaround this HW issue by avoiding writes to these registers for tonga asics. shill: remove ServicePropertyChangeNotifier This was only used for one property in Service, so we can simplify by replacing the change notifier with an implementation which just directly notifies about that one property and getting rid of all the boilerplate to support the unused general case. This includes PropertyObserver, which was only used by the ServicePropertyChangeNotifier, and its parent interface, which was only inherited by PropertyObserver and had no mocks or DI.
